lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: reproducing a drawing at a new scale
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: reproducing a drawing at a new scale

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: A 4 cm drawing represents 20 cm. What is the scale factor from drawing to actual?

steps: Write the scale as a ratio with matching units.
Multiply or divide consistently, then check whether the dimensions are possible.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: A map scale is 3 cm : 7 m. What actual distance does 39 cm represent?
A 22 m path is drawn at 1 cm : 2 m. What is its drawing length?
A 9 cm segment is reproduced using a scale factor of 7. What is its new length?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Can segments of lengths 5, 9, and 14 form a triangle?
choices: only if one angle is right

items.prompt: Which condition determines a unique triangle: SAS, SSA, AAA, or one side length?
A 9 cm drawing represents 72 cm. What is the scale factor from drawing to actual?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: A map scale is 1 cm : 3 m. What actual distance does 15 cm represent?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A 21 m path is drawn at 1 cm : 3 m. What is its drawing length?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
